title: State of AI Infrastructure & Energy
dek_2026: Measures the physical build-out behind AI: accelerator revenue and supply, data-centre capacity, electricity and water use, power contracts and GPU rental prices, for 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date.

2024: Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $115.2 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2025, which approximates calendar 2024, up 142% on the prior year.
The International Energy Agency estimates that data centres worldwide used about 415 terawatt-hours of electricity in 2024, roughly 1.5% of global electricity consumption.
Microsoft agreed on 20 September 2024 to buy the full output of Constellation's 835-megawatt Three Mile Island Unit 1 reactor for 20 years, the largest tech-company nuclear deal announced that year.
CBRE reported that vacancy across North America's primary data-centre markets fell to a record-low 2.8% in the first half of 2024, with a record 3,872 megawatts under construction.
By October 2024 Nvidia H100 GPUs were being rented on resale markets for about $2 per GPU-hour, down from around $8 during the 2023 shortage, according to an analysis published by Latent Space.
2025: Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $193.7 billion for its fiscal year ended January 2026, up 68%, within total revenue of $215.9 billion.

The IEA estimates that global data-centre electricity use rose to about 485 terawatt-hours in 2025, with consumption by AI-focused data centres up about 50%; Gartner puts the same year at 447 terawatt-hours.
OpenAI's chief financial officer said on 18 January 2026 that the company ended 2025 with about 1.9 gigawatts of compute, up from 0.6 gigawatts at the end of 2024.
Amazon signed a 1,920-megawatt nuclear power purchase agreement with Talen Energy's Susquehanna plant in June 2025, running to 2042 and worth about $18 billion to Talen.
PJM's capacity auction held in July 2025 cleared at its $329.17 per megawatt-day cap for the 2026/27 delivery year, up 22% from $269.92 a year earlier, as data-centre load forecasts rose.
2026: Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $89.0 billion for the quarter ended 26 July 2026, up 117% year on year, bringing the first half of its fiscal 2027 to $164.2 billion.

AMD reported Data Center segment revenue of $8.5 billion for the third quarter of 2026, up 97% year on year, and Broadcom reported AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion for its quarter to 2 August 2026, up 221%.

Gartner forecast on 10 June 2026 that global data-centre electricity consumption will reach 565 terawatt-hours in 2026, up 26%, with AI-optimised servers using about 175 terawatt-hours, or 31% of the total.
Meta announced on 9 January 2026 agreements for up to 6.6 gigawatts of nuclear power by 2035 from Vistra's existing plants and from TerraPower and Oklo reactors not yet built.
CBRE reported that North American primary-market data-centre vacancy fell to 1.4% in the first half of 2026, with a record 7,481 megawatts under construction and 80.4% of it already preleased.

2024: 2024 was the year AI infrastructure became a chip story first. Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $115.2 billion in the fiscal year ended January 2025, more than double the prior year, while AMD's Data Center segment grew 94% to $12.6 billion and Broadcom's AI revenue rose 220% to $12.2 billion. Supply, not demand, set the pace: TSMC ended the year with only about 35,000 wafers a month of CoWoS packaging capacity, the step that joins GPUs to high-bandwidth memory. TrendForce estimates AI server shipments rose 46%. The revenue is concentrated in one supplier, so any reading of 2024 is largely a reading of Nvidia's order book.

The energy debate started from small numbers. The IEA puts global data-centre use at about 415 TWh in 2024, roughly 1.5% of world electricity, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory put US data centres at 176 TWh, or 4.4% of national consumption, in 2023. What changed in 2024 was the forecast, not the measurement: LBNL's December report projected 325–580 TWh for the US by 2028. Per-query estimates were still dominated by a 2.9 Wh figure for a ChatGPT request, a top-down number later shown to be roughly ten times too high for typical prompts.

Power procurement moved from renewable certificates to firm supply. Microsoft's September deal to restart the 835 MW Three Mile Island Unit 1 reactor and Google's October agreement for 500 MW of future Kairos small reactors marked the first time hyperscalers paid to bring nuclear capacity back or into being. Grid prices began to reflect the queue: PJM's July 2024 auction cleared at $269.92 per MW-day for the 2025/26 delivery year, with two data-centre-heavy zones above $440. Meanwhile the GPU rental market cooled; resale H100s fell to about $2 an hour by October as 2023's shortage-era contracts came back onto the market.
2025: Chip revenue kept compounding in 2025, but its mix began to shift. Nvidia's data-centre revenue rose 68% to $193.7 billion in the fiscal year ended January 2026, while Broadcom's custom-accelerator and networking business reached about $20 billion and AMD's Data Center segment grew 32% to $16.6 billion. The slower growth at AMD reflects its CPU-heavy segment and export limits on MI308 sales to China. CoWoS capacity roughly doubled to 75,000–80,000 wafers a month by year end. Nvidia's lead remained wide, but the faster growth rates now sat with custom silicon designed for a single cloud customer.

Capacity announcements outran capacity. Stargate launched in January as a $500 billion private commitment and by September counted nearly 7 GW planned, yet OpenAI said it ended the year with about 1.9 GW of compute actually available, up from 0.6 GW. On the ground, CBRE's primary North American markets reached a record-low 1.6% vacancy in the first half, with 5,243 MW under construction. The IEA estimates global data-centre electricity rose to about 485 TWh, with AI-focused facilities up about 50%; Gartner's estimate for the same year is lower, at 447 TWh.

Power became the visible constraint. Amazon's 1,920 MW contract with Talen and Meta's 1,121 MW deal for Clinton's output showed hyperscalers locking up existing nuclear plants for twenty years. PJM's July auction cleared at its $329.17 cap, and its December auction at a $333.44 cap, transmitting data-centre demand into household capacity charges. Per-prompt evidence improved: Google's August disclosure of 0.24 Wh and 0.26 mL of water for a median Gemini text prompt gave the first full-stack vendor measurement. GPU rental prices drifted down through most of the year, reaching $2.00 an hour on Silicon Data's index in December.
2026: To date, 2026 is the largest year on record for AI chip revenue and the first in which every major vendor is growing at triple-digit or near-triple-digit rates. Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $164.2 billion in the six months to 26 July, nearly matching its whole fiscal 2025, and the latest quarter was $89.0 billion, up 117%. Broadcom's AI revenue was $35.9 billion in three quarters and AMD's Data Center segment $21.0 billion, both already above their 2025 totals. These are reported revenues, not shipments into operating data centres, and some of the buyers' purchases are financed by the sellers.

The gap between contracted and operating capacity is the central uncertainty of the year. OpenAI said in April that it had secured 10 GW of US capacity, five times the 1.9 GW it operated at the end of 2025, yet Epoch AI's satellite estimates put its flagship Abilene campus at about 421 MW of IT power in July, against 1.2 GW planned. CBRE's primary markets show the physical build: 7,481 MW under construction, 80.4% preleased and vacancy at 1.4%. Contracted gigawatts describe intent; megawatts energised describe what can run models.

Electricity is now a binding input rather than a footnote. Gartner forecasts data-centre consumption of 565 TWh in 2026, up 26%, with AI-optimised servers at about 175 TWh, and expects them to overtake conventional servers in 2027. EPRI's February update projects US data centres at 9–17% of national electricity by 2030, from 4–5% in 2024. PJM's July auction cleared at its cap for the third consecutive time and still fell about 6,831 MW short of its reliability target, the clearest market signal that supply is not keeping pace with new load.

Two price signals point in opposite directions. Compute is getting dearer per hour: Silicon Data's H100 rental index rose from $2.00 in December 2025 to $2.88 by 24 October 2026, about 44%, as demand for inference absorbed older GPUs. Energy per prompt is getting cheaper: a 2026 Microsoft Research study puts a typical query at a median 0.31 Wh, close to Google's 0.24 Wh, while long reasoning responses use about 3.9 Wh. Fleet electricity therefore depends more on how much reasoning-style work grows than on per-prompt efficiency. No company yet publishes the share of its queries that are reasoning-style, so that driver cannot be measured directly.

takeaways_2026: Nvidia's data-centre revenue reached $164.2 billion in the six months to 26 July 2026, and Broadcom's AI revenue ($35.9 billion in three quarters) and AMD's Data Center segment ($21.0 billion in three quarters) have already passed their full-year 2025 totals.

Contracted capacity far exceeds operating capacity: OpenAI reports 10 GW secured (April 2026) against about 1.9 GW available at the end of 2025, and Epoch AI estimates its Abilene campus was running about 421 MW in July 2026.

Electricity is the binding constraint: Gartner forecasts 565 TWh of data-centre consumption in 2026 (+26%), and PJM's July 2026 capacity auction cleared at its $325/MW-day cap while falling about 6,831 MW short of its reliability requirement.

GPU-hours are getting more expensive while prompts get cheaper: the H100 rental index rose about 44% from December 2025 to October 2026, while a typical text prompt is now measured at about 0.24–0.31 Wh.
yoy_takeaways: Nvidia's data-centre revenue went from $115.2 billion (FY ending Jan 2025) to $193.7 billion (FY ending Jan 2026) to $164.2 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027 alone; custom silicon grew faster, with Broadcom's AI revenue going from $12.2 billion to about $20 billion to $35.9 billion in three quarters.

North American primary-market vacancy fell from 2.8% (H1 2024) to 1.6% (H1 2025) to 1.4% (H1 2026) while capacity under construction nearly doubled from 3,872 MW to 7,481 MW: building faster has not loosened the market.

The scale of power deals grew roughly eightfold in two years, from Microsoft's 835 MW reactor restart (2024) to Amazon's 1,920 MW Talen contract (2025) to Meta's 6.6 GW nuclear package (2026), and PJM capacity prices rose from $269.92 to the $325–333 cap.

H100 rental prices fell from about $8 an hour (2023) to about $2 (late 2024 and December 2025), then rose to about $2.88 (October 2026), a reversal that marks the shift from training-led to inference-led demand.

faq_2026.q: How much electricity do data centres use in 2026?
faq_2026.a: No measured 2026 total exists yet. Gartner forecast on 10 June 2026 that global data-centre electricity consumption will reach 565 TWh in 2026, up 26% from 447 TWh in 2025. The IEA estimates 2025 consumption at about 485 TWh (April 2026 update) and projects about 950 TWh by 2030, just under 3% of global electricity. The two organisations draw the boundary of a data centre differently, which is why their 2025 figures differ by about 40 TWh.

faq_2026.q: How fast is Nvidia's data-centre business growing in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Nvidia reported data-centre revenue of $89.0 billion for the quarter ended 26 July 2026, up 117% year on year and 18% on the prior quarter. The first two quarters of fiscal 2027 (February to July 2026) total $164.2 billion, compared with $193.7 billion for the whole of fiscal 2026 and $115.2 billion for fiscal 2025. Nvidia guided total revenue for the quarter to October 2026 to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

faq_2026.q: How much AI data-centre capacity is actually running?
faq_2026.a: Far less than has been announced. OpenAI said it ended 2025 with about 1.9 GW of compute and in April 2026 said it had secured 10 GW, which reporting reads as contracted rather than operating. Epoch AI's satellite tracker estimated the flagship Stargate site in Abilene, Texas, at about 421 MW of IT power in late July 2026, against a planned 1.2 GW. CBRE counted 7,481 MW under construction in North America's primary markets in the first half of 2026.

faq_2026.q: How much energy and water does one AI prompt use?
faq_2026.a: Google reported in August 2025 that a median Gemini text prompt uses 0.24 Wh of electricity and 0.26 mL of water. A 2026 Microsoft Research study in Joule estimates a median 0.31 Wh for a typical chatbot response of about 300 tokens and 3.91 Wh for a long reasoning response. The 2.9 Wh figure widely quoted since 2024 is an older top-down estimate roughly ten times higher than current measurements of typical prompts.

faq_2026.q: What does it cost to rent an Nvidia H100 GPU in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Silicon Data's H100 rental index (ticker SDH100RT) read about $2.88 per GPU-hour on 24 October 2026 and ranged from $2.81 to $2.97 between 7 October and 5 November 2026, up about 44% from its $2.00 low on 9 December 2025. Hyperscaler on-demand list prices are much higher, about $10–12 per GPU-hour at Oracle and Azure, and neocloud on-demand list prices had a median of about $4.20 in October 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: A ChatGPT query uses about 2.9 Wh, ten times a Google search.
stop_quoting.fact: That is a 2023–24 top-down estimate. Google measured 0.24 Wh for a median Gemini text prompt (Aug 2025), and a 2026 Microsoft Research study puts a typical query at a median 0.31 Wh; long reasoning responses are about 3.9 Wh.

stop_quoting.claim: OpenAI now runs 10 gigawatts of compute.
stop_quoting.fact: OpenAI said in April 2026 it had secured 10 GW of US capacity; reporting reads this as contracted. The company said it ended 2025 with about 1.9 GW available.

stop_quoting.claim: Stargate is a $500 billion US government programme.
stop_quoting.fact: Stargate is a private joint venture (OpenAI, Oracle, SoftBank, MGX). The federal role at the Ohio site is a leased former DOE facility and permitting, not appropriated money.

stop_quoting.claim: Nvidia is guaranteeing $250 billion of Stargate debt.
stop_quoting.fact: Nvidia's guarantee for the Ohio site was cut to up to $105 billion in August 2026 and covers only phase one (~5 GW); chip financing of up to ~$350 billion is separate.

stop_quoting.claim: US data centres will use 12% of US electricity by 2028.
stop_quoting.fact: 12% is the top of LBNL's 6.7–12% scenario range for 2028 (325–580 TWh), not a forecast. EPRI's 2026 update gives 9–17% by 2030, also as scenarios.

stop_quoting.claim: xAI's Colossus 2 became the world's first gigawatt AI training cluster in January 2026.
stop_quoting.fact: This is Elon Musk's claim (17 Jan 2026). Satellite analysis of cooling capacity suggested roughly 350 MW at the time; independent confirmation of 1 GW was not found.

stop_quoting.claim: Nvidia has 94% of the AI chip market.
stop_quoting.fact: 94% is Jon Peddie Research's Q4 2025 share of add-in-board GPUs, mostly gaming cards. Estimates of Nvidia's AI accelerator revenue share in 2026 range from about 70–75% (Bloomberg Intelligence, forecast) to about 85% (Morgan Stanley).
